title: Guard battery sysfs rate against bogus EC readings
head: cd81d771454f
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: A brief sampled hold does not reset the charge-delta series
leads.consequence: Even with the panel open at its normal 5-second interval, an intervening pending-charge, fully-charged or unknown state is not recorded. If discharging resumes within 45 seconds, old samples survive; at 35 seconds from the previous discharge but just 25 seconds from resumption, the panel and notification display an 8.6W/3h 16m estimate using charge measured across the hold. On subsequent runs the old row remains until max-window pruning. Record a state discontinuity or invalidate the cache on all sampleable-to-nonsampleable transitions, not only a time gap.
leads.triage: corroborated: Opus residual table (pending-charge 30 s); in public Limit line

leads.summary: Energy-unit ACPI batteries cannot use the charge-delta fallback
leads.consequence: The kernel exposes energy_now/power_now instead of charge_now/current_now for an ACPI battery reporting mWh rather than mAh. When power_now is implausible and UPower still reports 0W, sampleable stays false even while energy_now declines; no fallback rate or remaining time appears until UPower itself recovers. Sample energy_now deltas as a separate unit family without the voltage multiplier when charge_now is absent.
leads.triage: corroborated: Opus R3 note; unchanged, not repeated publicly

leads.summary: The only sparse caller can never build a rate estimate
leads.consequence: With the panel closed, a user invoking only the battery notification or CLI at least 46 seconds apart resets the entire cache on every call. The displayed rate stays 0W and the time remains blank even during a steady discharge. A 45-second gap protects against suspend but is shorter than the 120-second window; either separate suspend/state detection from sparse polling or retain safe, monotonic samples across ordinary caller gaps.

leads.summary: Open PR #13111 requires a rate the current guard rejects
leads.consequence: #13111 tests that 60W sysfs with 8W UPower must display 60W to preserve a fast load step; this PR treats 60 > 3*8 as implausible and displays 8W. Both merge-file copies have unresolved conflict markers, in script and test; merely choosing either hunk makes the other PR's expectation fail. Align the guard and mutually exclusive tests before merging both.
leads.triage: corroborated: Opus notes conflict; public one-line note

leads.summary: The malformed-cache regression test does not exercise voltage validation
leads.consequence: The new test corrupts charge but always supplies valid voltage. If the cached-voltage check is accidentally removed, the entire PR test still passes; a missing or malformed voltage could then reach avg_volt arithmetic. Add a recent record with numeric charge and missing/non-numeric voltage, verify no diagnostics and the record is omitted from the rewritten cache.
leads.triage: corroborated: Opus F1; public optional test note

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** The 45 s reset also fires after the panel is closed for over 45 s, so quick glances show no estimate.

**Earlier findings** ([review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13009#issuecomment-5855375133), rechecked at `cd81d77` after the author's reply): all resolved (window across suspend, holds and swaps for gaps over 45 s; cache validation; time to full; test).

### Reopening the panel after 45 s restarts the estimate

When UPower is wedged and sysfs rejected, a reopen after 45 s shows `0W` and no time for 30 s. A hotkey press gets an estimate only if the script ran 30 to 45 s earlier. `05f1edc` estimated on the first refresh; the base never estimates, so this is not a regression.

**Suggested change:** Keep history across ordinary closes (for example resetting on resume, not elapsed time), or document this cost at `bin/omarchy-battery-status:102-104`.

<details><summary>Reproducer (sandboxed run at cd81d77 and 05f1edc)</summary>

# Reproducer: the 45 s reset also discards history between panel openings

Reviewed head: `cd81d771454f9c4349fb59d72ea5e6b7c7367c75`. Compared with `05f1edc`.

This is the behaviour the author accepted ("0W for the first 30s after any
gap"); the reproducer shows that an ordinary panel close counts as such a gap.

## PR-style snippet

Appended to `test/shell.d/battery-status-test.sh` before the final `rg`
check (reuses the `wedge` fixture: UPower 0 W, sysfs current -65 A,
`charge_now` 4600000, 12 V, `date +%s` = 1800000060):

```bash
# Steady 7.5 W (19 mAh in 110 s), last refresh 60 s ago, panel reopened now.
printf 'BAT0 discharging 1799999950 4619000 12000000\n' >"$tmp_dir/reopen.cache"
printf 'BAT0 discharging 1800000000 4610000 12000000\n' >>"$tmp_dir/reopen.cache"
reopen_output=$(OMARCHY_POWER_SUPPLY_PATH="$tmp_dir/wedge/power" OMARCHY_BATTERY_CACHE="$tmp_dir/reopen.cache" PATH="$tmp_dir/wedge/bin:$PATH" "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-battery-status" --shell)
printf 'REPRO reopen: %s | %s\n' "$(grep $'^rate\t' <<<"$reopen_output")" "$(grep $'^time\t' <<<"$reopen_output")"
```

Actual output (sandboxed run):

```
cd81d77:  REPRO reopen: rate	0W | time	
05f1edc:  REPRO reopen: rate	7.5W | time	3h 47m
```

## Timelines (actual script, stubbed UPower at 0 W and clock, 12 V, 1 mAh steps, 7.5 W load)

Panel open 20 s (refresh every 5 s), closed, then reopened:

| Closed for | `cd81d77` first 30 s after reopening | `05f1edc` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 20 s | `7.6W` to `8W` from the first refresh | same |
| 40 s | `7.6W` to `8.1W` from the first refresh | same |
| 60 s | `0W`, no time, for refreshes at 0 to 25 s; `8.6W` at 30 s | `7.6W` to `7.9W` from the first refresh |
| 300 s | `0W`, no time, for 0 to 25 s; `7.2W` at 30 s | `7.5W` to `7.6W` from the first refresh |

Single invocations (the `Super+Ctrl+Alt+B` notification runs the script once):

| Calls | `cd81d77` | `05f1edc` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| t=0, t=300 s | `0W`, `0W` | `0W`, `7.6W` |
| t=0, t=35 s | `0W`, `8.6W` | same |

Periodic caller, 600 s at 7.5 W:

| Interval | `cd81d77` calls with an estimate | `05f1edc` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 30 s | 20 of 21 | 20 of 21 |
| 45 s | 13 of 14 | 13 of 14 |
| 50 s | 0 of 13 | 12 of 13 |
| 60 s | 0 of 11 | 10 of 11 |

The base branch never estimates. With the same fixture (UPower 0 W, sysfs
current -65 A at 12 V) the merge-base script `d3cfd53` printed `-780W` with an
empty time on every call, because it uses any readable sysfs reading
(`bin/omarchy-battery-status:50-57` at `d3cfd53`). So this is not a regression
against `quattro`; it narrows the fallback's benefit relative to `05f1edc`.
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified:**
- Suspend 180 s, AC hold 180 s and a same-slot swap with 60 s absent now give `0W` until the 30 s refresh, then within 15% of the actual rate (synthetic 10 W and 30 W loads).
- Cache lines with a command substitution, `46abc` or a missing voltage are dropped at 35 s old; no cache is written when neither `OMARCHY_BATTERY_CACHE` nor `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is set.
- Time to full uses untruncated `energy-full` (`9m` in the new test), matching UPower's formula.
- The full `./test/shell` fails the same files at `cd81d77` and the merge base; none involve this script.

**Limit:** Interruptions of 45 s or less are still measured across (40 s suspend at 10 W: `6.8W`, within 15% after 80 s), so the comment's "can never borrow a reading" holds only for longer gaps.

**Suggested change, other options:** A background sampler would also keep history across closes. An AC hold or pack swap while the panel is closed leaves nothing a non-running script can observe, so each option has its own cost.

**Optional test improvement:** The identity and stale-cache tests seed samples older than 45 s, which the reset would discard anyway. Mutants without the identity check, with a 600 s window or without the voltage check pass the head test file; the block below catches each.

# Reproducer: tests no longer isolate three cache guards at cd81d77

Reviewed head: `cd81d771454f9c4349fb59d72ea5e6b7c7367c75`.

## 1. Mutants that pass the unmodified `test/shell.d/battery-status-test.sh`

Each mutant is `bin/omarchy-battery-status` at `cd81d77` with one change; the
test file is the one at `cd81d77`, run with `bash test/shell.d/battery-status-test.sh`.

| Mutant | Change | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| no identity check | delete line 135 (`[[ $sample_battery == "$native_path" && $sample_state == "$state" ]] \|\| continue`) | exit 0, `ok - battery status owns capacity and remaining calculations` |
| 600 s window | `maximum_window=120` becomes `maximum_window=600` | exit 0, same `ok` line |
| no window filter | delete line 138 (`(( now_ts - sample_ts <= maximum_window )) \|\| continue`) | exit 0, same `ok` line |
| charge-only check | line 137 checks only `$sample_charge` | exit 0, same `ok` line |

The same identity mutant applied to the `05f1edc` script, run against the
`05f1edc` test file, fails:

```
not ok - battery status ignores samples from another battery
not ok - battery status ignores samples from another state
```

Why: the identity and stale-cache tests seed samples 60 s and 1060 s old
(`1800000000`, `1799999000` with the clock stubbed at `1800000060`). The new
`reset_gap=45` (line 148) discards any history whose newest sample is older
than 45 s, so these samples would be discarded even without the identity or
window check (at `cd81d77` those checks, lines 135 and 138, still run first).

The non-numeric test (line 127) seeds a sample 5 s old, below the 30 s
`minimum_window`, so the estimate loop never evaluates it. Without the numeric
guard, its `rate 0W` assertion (line 129) still passes; only the carry-forward
check (line 130) fails:

```
not ok - battery status drops non-numeric cache samples
```

## 2. Test additions that do isolate them

Insert before the final `rg` check in `test/shell.d/battery-status-test.sh`
(reuses the file's `wedge` fixture: UPower 0 W, sysfs current -65 A,
`charge_now` 4600000, 12 V, `date +%s` = 1800000060):

```bash
# Identity samples 35s old, so the 45s gap reset cannot be what drops them.
printf 'BAT1 discharging 1800000025 4609000 12000000\n' >"$tmp_dir/other35.cache"
other35_output=$(OMARCHY_POWER_SUPPLY_PATH="$tmp_dir/wedge/power" OMARCHY_BATTERY_CACHE="$tmp_dir/other35.cache" PATH="$tmp_dir/wedge/bin:$PATH" "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-battery-status" --shell)
grep -Fx $'rate\t0W' <<<"$other35_output" >/dev/null || fail "battery status ignores a 35s-old sample from another battery" "$other35_output"
printf 'BAT0 charging 1800000025 4609000 12000000\n' >"$tmp_dir/state35.cache"
state35_output=$(OMARCHY_POWER_SUPPLY_PATH="$tmp_dir/wedge/power" OMARCHY_BATTERY_CACHE="$tmp_dir/state35.cache" PATH="$tmp_dir/wedge/bin:$PATH" "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-battery-status" --shell)
grep -Fx $'rate\t0W' <<<"$state35_output" >/dev/null || fail "battery status ignores a 35s-old sample from another state" "$state35_output"

# A sample chain longer than 120s; the reference must be the oldest sample inside 120s.
printf 'BAT0 discharging 1799999920 4620000 12000000\n' >"$tmp_dir/window.cache"
printf 'BAT0 discharging 1799999960 4610000 12000000\n' >>"$tmp_dir/window.cache"
printf 'BAT0 discharging 1800000000 4606000 12000000\n' >>"$tmp_dir/window.cache"
printf 'BAT0 discharging 1800000040 4602000 12000000\n' >>"$tmp_dir/window.cache"
window_output=$(OMARCHY_POWER_SUPPLY_PATH="$tmp_dir/wedge/power" OMARCHY_BATTERY_CACHE="$tmp_dir/window.cache" PATH="$tmp_dir/wedge/bin:$PATH" "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-battery-status" --shell)
grep -Fx $'rate\t4.3W' <<<"$window_output" >/dev/null || fail "battery status measures within the 120s maximum window" "$window_output"

# A sample old enough to reach the arithmetic, with its voltage missing.
printf 'BAT0 discharging 1800000025 4609000\n' >"$tmp_dir/novolt.cache"
novolt_output=$(OMARCHY_POWER_SUPPLY_PATH="$tmp_dir/wedge/power" OMARCHY_BATTERY_CACHE="$tmp_dir/novolt.cache" PATH="$tmp_dir/wedge/bin:$PATH" "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-battery-status" --shell)
grep -Fx $'rate\t0W' <<<"$novolt_output" >/dev/null || fail "battery status ignores a sample without a voltage" "$novolt_output"
```

## 3. Actual results (sandboxed runs, continue-on-failure copy of the test)

| Script | Failing assertions (rate printed) |
| --- | --- |
| `cd81d77` unchanged | none; stock run exits 0 |
| no identity check | 35s-old sample from another battery (`rate 11.1W`); from another state (`rate 11.1W`) |
| 600 s window | 120s maximum window (`rate 6.2W`) |
| no window filter | 120s maximum window (`rate 6.2W`) |
| charge-only check | sample without a voltage (`rate 5.6W`) |
| no numeric check | drops non-numeric cache samples; sample without a voltage (`rate 5.6W`) |

Expected values: 9000 uAh over 35 s at 12 V is 11.1 W; 10000 uAh over 100 s
is 4.3 W, 20000 uAh over 140 s is 6.2 W; a missing voltage halves the average
voltage, giving 5.6 W.

**Note:** Open PR #13111 still conflicts in both files.
</details>
